segments.text: This paper asks whether the earliest gas-metallicity deficit survives two common weak points: gravitational lensing and an extrapolated local comparison. It isolates unlensed field galaxies and repeats the calculation against two local anchors.
The core Pollock sample contains five direct electron-temperature galaxies at redshifts 9.3 to 9.9. Their stellar masses sit near ten to the 8.2 through 8.6 solar-mass range.
Against the Curti local relation, the unlensed sample lies 0.69 plus or minus 0.03 dex lower in oxygen abundance. Leaving out one galaxy at a time changes the result by only 0.04 dex.
Replacing the extrapolated Curti relation with the measured direct-Te relation from Andrews and Martini changes the deficit by only 0.04 dex, from minus 0.69 to minus 0.65.
An independent stacked direct-Te analysis of roughly fifteen hundred JADES galaxies gives a 0.5 to 0.6 dex deficit. It uses a different method and spans redshifts four through ten.

The absolute electron-temperature abundance scale still carries a roughly 0.1 to 0.2 dex systematic floor. This is a descriptive machine-generated draft, not a validated measurement and not a formal statistical detection.
